query: For high-entropy alloys intended for structural applications, what testable methodological hypothesis could enable improved combinations of strength, ductility, Young’s modulus, and fracture resistance? Explain why it should work, what measurable improvement is expected relative to the state of the art, the conditions under which it should or should not hold, the prior evidence supporting it, and an experimental result that would decisively falsify it.

generation.hypothesis: Introducing a stable hetero-lamellar microstructure composed of alternating ultrafine-grained (UFG, ~0.2–0.8 µm) and coarse-grained (CG, 5–15 µm) layers into the equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi high-entropy alloy (Cantor alloy) by accumulative roll bonding (ARB) followed by partial recrystallisation annealing will simultaneously raise yield strength, ultimate tensile strength, Young’s modulus and plane-strain fracture toughness while retaining high ductility. The key assertion is that back-stress hardening generated at interfaces between the UFG and CG lamellae will roughly triple the yield strength (to ≈900 MPa) yet still allow ≥30 % uniform elongation and ≥150 MPa√m fracture toughness at ambient temperature, with a modest (≈5 %) increase in Young’s modulus relative to the homogenised, coarse-grained state.
generation.material_initial_state: Equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi high-entropy alloy in the homogenised (1100 °C, 1 h, water-quenched) coarse-grained single-phase FCC condition (average grain size ≈ 50 µm; σ0.2 ≈ 300 MPa, UTS ≈ 600 MPa, uniform elongation ≈ 45 %, K_IC ≈ 90 MPa√m, E ≈ 200 GPa).
generation.intervention: Five cycles of accumulative roll bonding with 50 % thickness reduction per cycle at 400 °C, followed by a short (10 min) anneal at 650 °C to trigger partial recrystallisation without full grain growth, producing ~alternate 20–40 µm thick CG and UFG lamellae through the sheet thickness.
generation.conditions: Process in vacuum-sealed cans to suppress oxidation; room-temperature monotonic tension and compact-tension fracture tests at strain rate 10⁻³ s⁻¹; ambient environment; thickness ≤3 mm so through-thickness gradient is uniform.
generation.structural_mediator: High density of hetero-interfaces between UFG and CG lamellae that store geometrically necessary dislocations and generate large back-stresses during deformation, plus retained nanoscale deformation twins inside UFG layers.
generation.mechanism:
1. Strength: UFG lamellae offer Hall–Petch strengthening; dislocation pile-ups at CG/UFG interfaces create back-stress that elevates the overall flow stress.
2. Ductility & toughness: CG lamellae accommodate strain by dislocation glide and twin formation, delaying localization; back-stress hardening raises strain-hardening capacity, postponing necking.
3. Young’s modulus: The high dislocation and twin density in UFG lamellae, together with elastic constraint from CG layers, increases the effective modulus by ~5 %.
4. Fracture resistance: Constrained plasticity of UFG layers plus crack-deflection at lamellar interfaces increases crack-tip blunting and R-curve, doubling K_IC.
generation.predicted_outcome:
Compared with the baseline homogenised alloy, the processed hetero-lamellar material will show at 298 K:
• Yield strength (0.2 % offset) ≈ 900 ± 100 MPa (≥3× baseline).
• Ultimate tensile strength ≈ 1100 ± 100 MPa.
• Uniform elongation ≥ 30 % (≥⅔ of baseline despite tripled strength).
• Young’s modulus ≈ 210 ± 10 GPa (≈5 % higher).
• Plane-strain fracture toughness K_IC ≥ 150 MPa√m (≥60 % higher).
generation.baseline: Homogenised coarse-grained CoCrFeMnNi (σ0.2 ≈ 300 MPa; UTS ≈ 600 MPa; ε_uniform ≈ 45 %; K_IC ≈ 90 MPa√m; E ≈ 200 GPa).
generation.boundary:
1. Fewer than three ARB cycles or annealing above 700 °C eliminates the hetero-lamellar structure, negating benefits.
2. At test temperatures >400 °C, dynamic recovery will reduce back-stress hardening, diminishing strength–ductility synergy.
3. Sheets thicker than ~5 mm may develop non-uniform deformation during ARB, reducing property improvements.
generation.uncertainty: Magnitude of modulus increase is least certain; stiffening may be <5 % if elastic mismatch between lamellae is small. Excessive residual stresses or interface damage from ARB could lower toughness, offsetting predicted gains.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two 2 mm-thick Cantor alloy sheet sets: (A) homogenised reference; (B) subjected to the specified 5-cycle ARB + 650 °C/10 min anneal. Characterise microstructure (EBSD grain maps, TEM for UFG lamellae and twins). Perform room-temperature tensile tests (ASTM E8) and compact-tension fracture toughness tests (ASTM E399). Measure Young’s modulus via resonant ultrasound spectroscopy.
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If sample B fails to achieve BOTH (i) σ0.2 ≥ 600 MPa AND (ii) uniform elongation ≥ 20 %, or if microstructural analysis shows absence of distinct alternating UFG/CG lamellae after processing, the hypothesis is falsified.
